Diptychon vs Marta, ForkLift, Nimble & Path Finder

There's no clear winner among Mac file managers — this segment tool-hops for a reason. Here's an honest read of where Diptychon fits, and where these (genuinely good) tools still beat it.

Diptychon is a fast, keyboard-first dual-panel file manager: native, ~1.4 MB, one-time purchase, no telemetry, undo anything. It's pre-launch — this page is about fit, not a claim that it's finished.

Where each one wins (honestly)

Marta

Wins: free, keyboard-cult-favorite, native and plain-fast. Diptychon's edge: undo-anything and real Finder tags, plus an actively-shipped roadmap — Marta's recurring community worry is single-developer continuity, not capability.

ForkLift 4

Wins: the remote powerhouse (SFTP/FTP/WebDAV/S3/cloud/SMB), folder sync, multi-rename — and a fair one-time $19.95. Diptychon's edge: ~1.4 MB vs ~16 MB and keyboard-first — if all you need is local, ForkLift is a lot of app.

Nimble Commander

Wins: blazing C++ speed, 100+ hotkeys, remote mounts, open-source. Diptychon's edge: gentler to learn (Nimble's curve is steep), no feature paywall in the free build, undo, native Finder tags.

Path Finder

Wins: the deepest, kitchen-sink power-feature set, still actively maintained. Diptychon's edge: Path Finder now runs on a yearly subscription (~$32.95/yr) — Diptychon's planned one-time purchase and tiny footprint is the clean contrast if you're done renting software.

Diptychon is for you if…

  • You live in the keyboard and Finder feels slow.
  • You want native + tiny, not a web wrapper.
  • One-time purchase, no telemetry matters to you.
  • You mostly work on local (or mounted) drives.

Look elsewhere if…

  • Your core job is remote servers → ForkLift or Nimble.
  • You want the deepest feature set → Path Finder.
  • Free-forever is a hard requirement → Marta.
